newsitem.title: USA: Newmont Gold wins Yanacocha mine lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Newmont Gold wins Yanacocha mine lawsuit.

text.p: Newmont Gold Co said it and Compania de Minas Buenaventura have had their bid to take a larger stake in the Yanacocha gold mine upheld by a Peruvian court.

"Newmont Gold and Compania de Minas Buenaventura have been advised that the Eighth Court of the Superior Court of Lima has upheld the decision of the Fifth Civil Court of Lima regarding ownership rights to Minera Yanacocha in Peru," Newmont said in a statement.

The ruling confirms the right of Newmont and Buenaventura to exercise their preemptive rights to acquire a 24.7 percent stake in the mine which was originally held by BRGM, an agency of the French government.
Last September the Peru civil court set a purchase price of $109.3 million for the 24.7 percent stake, of which Newmont's share is approximately $59 million.

Newmont's stake in the mine will now rise to 51.35 percent from 38 percent, adds 815,000 ounces to the Denver based company's proven and probable reserves, and 685,000 ounces to mineralized material not in reserves.
"In addition, it will increase production in 1997 by an estimated 100,000 ounces and add significantly to earnings," Newmont said.
As a result of the ruling, Newmont will account for Yanacocha on a consolidated basis. Until now, Newmont said it accounted for its 38 percent interest in the mine on an equity basis.
Newmont said issues in the lawsuit did not qualify for any further review by a higher court.
Yanacocha is the largest gold mine in Latin America, producing 81,400 ounces in 1996 at a total cash cost of $107 per ounce.
At the end of last year, the mine had proven and probable reserves of 6 million ounces and mineralized material not in reserves in excess of 5 million ounces.
